title: Share your coat (Luke 3:1–20)
hook: John tells soldiers and tax collectors to be fair and share

segments.voice: Yesterday, the boy Jesus was lost and found in the Temple, and then he grew. Your line was growing is holy. A new week starts.

Luke opens chapter three like a historian dating a document. In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar. Pontius Pilate governor of Judea. Herod tetrarch of Galilee, his brother Philip tetrarch of the next region over, Lysanias of Abilina. Annas and Caiphas the high priests. A roll call of power, lined up in order. And then: the word of the Lord came to John, the son of Zachary, in the desert. Not to any of them. To a man in the wilderness.
screen: `THE FIFTEENTH YEAR OF TIBERIUS.` → `A ROLL CALL OF POWER, IN ORDER.` → `THE WORD CAME TO JOHN, IN THE DESERT.`

segments.voice: John comes into the country around the Jordan, preaching a baptism of penance for the forgiveness of sins, as Isaias had written: a voice of one crying in the wilderness, prepare ye the way of the Lord. Crowds come out to be baptized, and he doesn't flatter them. Brood of vipers, he calls them. Don't tell yourselves you're safe because Abraham is your father. The axe is already laid to the root of the trees. Shaken, the crowds ask: then what shall we do? His answer is surprisingly ordinary. In the Douay-Rheims: "He that hath two coats, let him give to him that hath none; and he that hath meat, let him do in like manner." The publicans, the tax collectors, ask: and us? Don't collect more than you're supposed to. Soldiers ask too: don't bully anyone, don't accuse anyone falsely, and be content with your pay. He doesn't tell the tax collectors to quit, or the soldiers to desert. He tells them to be honest and fair where they already are. The coat in his first answer is a chiton, the tunic worn under the outer cloak. If you have two, one is a spare. John's preaching points past himself, to one coming who is mightier, whose sandal strap he isn't worthy to untie. And Luke ends the scene with what that honesty cost him: Herod, rebuked by John, shut him up in prison.
screen: `A VOICE CRYING IN THE WILDERNESS.` · `THEN WHAT SHALL WE DO?` · `NOT QUIT: BE FAIR WHERE YOU ARE.` · `A CHITON: THE SPARE TUNIC.` · then, large: `HE THAT HATH TWO COATS, LET HIM GIVE.`

segments.voice: Picture your closet, or the hooks by your door, and go through it slowly in your mind until you find something warm you have two of, or haven't worn in a year. Think of where it could go: a shelter, a parish clothing drive, someone you know who's cold. Then ask the crowd's question about the rest of your life, what shall I do, right where I am, and if you pray, offer the answer to God.
chiton. Greek for the tunic worn under the cloak: John the Baptist told the crowds, whoever has two, give one to someone who has none. Today's word.
Your line: two coats, give one. Fair and honest, right where you are. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics hear John the Baptist's preaching in Advent, and some parishes run coat and clothing drives in winter; clothing the naked is one of the corporal works of mercy.

original.note: Greek: tunic, the garment worn under the outer cloak; Luke 3:11's 'coat'.

trapdoor: what you thought: John the Baptist was all fire and judgment.
what it means: when the crowds ask what to do, John's answers are ordinary and concrete: share the spare, be honest at work, don't bully.
what a scholar hears: chiton, the inner tunic; and Luke dates John's call the way ancient histories did, by the year of a ruler's reign.

chat.says: When John the Baptist told people to repent, what did he actually tell them to do?
options: Ordinary things: share your spare coat and food, take only what's fair, don't bully.
Quit their jobs as tax collectors and soldiers and follow him into the desert.
Fast for forty days in the wilderness before they could be baptized.
chat.meaning: John told the crowds to give a spare coat, tax collectors to collect no more than due, and soldiers not to bully. Be fair where you are.
